value.name: speaker promises to repeat explanation
value.description: The speaker says he will explain something now and again later because she will not understand it the first time.
evidence: ill tell you, and I also promise you that you will not listen the first time, and I promise you that I will tell you again."

value.name: she laughs at his remark
value.description: She responds with a brief, nearly silent laugh, signaling dry amusement or resignation.
evidence: She laughed once, short, almost soundless.

value.name: he acknowledges long employment
value.description: He tells her he knows her well because he has worked for her for six years.
evidence: "I know it's about right. I've worked for you for six years."

value.name: they drive in silence
value.description: The two of them finish the drive without speaking, marking a pause after the exchange.
evidence: They made the rest of the drive in silence.

value.name: she delivers petition and codicil
value.description: At the office, she brings Mr. Halloran the petition and the original codicil and places them on his desk.
evidence: At the office she went straight to Mr. Halloran's door and laid the petition on his desk and the original codicil, in its archival sleeve, on top of the petition.

value.name: halloran inspects codicil
value.description: Mr. Halloran studies the codicil carefully, reading it twice before speaking.
evidence: He looked at the codicil for a long time without touching it. He read it twice.

value.name: halloran confirms codicil validity
value.description: Halloran identifies the codicil as clean and self-proving, confirming its legal strength.

value.name: halloran questions missing codicil
value.description: Halloran asks why the codicil did not arrive with the rest of the file, raising the central mystery.
evidence: "Why did it not arrive with the rest of the file."

value.name: she suspects older brother
value.description: She tells Halloran she wants to know why the codicil was missing and implies the older brother may have removed it.
evidence: "That," she said, "is what I would like to know."
"You think the older brother removed it."
"I think he had the access, the motive, and the temperament. I cannot yet say he had the act."

value.name: halloran asks her to investigate
value.description: Halloran asks whether she will investigate the missing codicil, and she hesitates before answering.
evidence: She thought about this. She had thought about it, in fact, all the way down Spruce Street, and she had not yet arrived at an answer that satisfied her.

value.name: she declines immediate investigation
value.description: She decides not to pursue the missing-codicil question yet because the codicil has already been filed and the will amended of record.
